title: Dutch school holidays 2026-27 and extra leave (verlof)
desc: School holiday dates 2026-27 for the north, middle and south regions, plus the strict rules for extra leave (extra verlof) outside the holidays and how to ask.
h1: School holidays 2026-27 and taking your child out of school
lede: Dutch school holidays differ by region, and a family holiday outside them is normally not allowed. Extra leave (verlof) is possible only for a few reasons, the school head decides up to 10 days, and you must ask in time.

blocks.p: The Netherlands has three holiday regions: north (noord), middle (midden) and south (zuid). Each municipality is listed under one of them (a few are split by village, so check the Rijksoverheid list of regions). The national government sets the summer holiday, the Christmas holiday and one week in May. For the autumn and spring holidays it gives advisory dates. A school can choose other dates once its participation council (medezeggenschapsraad) agrees. Always check the school calendar.

blocks.note: Schools may add days, for example study days for staff, or a second May week (the advisory dates for it are 1 to 9 May 2027). In the south, a school may move the spring holiday to match carnival: the Rijksoverheid says the advisory spring dates do not fall on carnival in 2027 and that schools may choose other dates, for example to match it. Dates checked on the Rijksoverheid overview on 25 November 2026.

blocks.p: Each school page in [find a school](/find/) shows the holiday region of that school.

Once your child must attend school, you may not take your child on holiday outside the school holidays. This is the compulsory education law (leerplicht). It applies from the first day of the month after your child's fifth birthday. See [when a child must go to school](/questions/when-must-child-go/). A child of 4 may go to school but is not yet bound by it, so ask the school what it expects.
The rule does not depend on how long the trip is, how expensive the flights are or whether your child is doing well. Cheaper tickets or tickets you already bought are not a reason.
There are two routes. The school head (directeur) decides up to 10 school days.

ul: Work. Your job means you cannot take a family holiday in any school holiday of the year, for example seasonal work, or self-employment where travelling in the holidays would cost you a large part of your income. You can get up to 10 school days, once per school year, and not in the first 2 weeks after the summer holiday. Employees bring a statement from the employer. Self-employed parents must show the large income loss.

Special circumstances (gewichtige omstandigheden). Events outside your control that cannot be moved to another date, for example a funeral. Ask the school head. If you need more than 10 days, the request goes to the municipality's attendance officer (leerplichtambtenaar).

blocks.p: Ask the school or your municipality what counts as a special circumstance before you book. The Rijksoverheid names a funeral as an example and gives no full list. Municipalities publish their own guidance, for example The Hague on the page linked under the sources, with examples and a maximum number of days for each event. We could not confirm one national list, so read the guidance of your own municipality.

steps: Ask the school how it wants the request: a form or a letter.
Send it as early as you can. For leave because of work, the rule is at least 8 weeks before the first day of leave.
Give the dates, the reason and proof: an employer statement, proof of the income loss for self-employed parents (ask the school what it accepts), or a letter about the event.
Wait for the answer in writing before you book anything that cannot be refunded.
If the answer is no and you disagree, tell the school head in writing and ask for the reasons.

blocks.say: We would like to ask for leave from [date] to [date] because [reason]. Which documents do you need, and by when will we hear?

blocks.p: If you still disagree, ask the school or your municipality what else you can do.

sections.h: What happens if you go without permission

blocks.p: Going without permission can lead to a fine. We cannot give an amount: the Rijksoverheid does not state one. Parents can also be punished for keeping a child at home once compulsory education applies. Your municipality or the attendance officer can tell you more.

blocks.note: This guide gives general information, not legal advice. For your own case, ask the school, your municipality or Ouders & Onderwijs.
